CONTENT PREVIEW:
Feature: Scope service DB credentials per ControlPlane and database

# GitHub Issue #435: feat(c5c3-operator): scope service database credentials per ControlPlane and per database (drop the shared flat OpenBao path)

**Description:**

Today every Keystone instance draws its MariaDB user password from one shared, flat OpenBao secret. The Keystone DB password lives at the unscoped KV-v2 path `openstack/keystone/db`, materialised into a single Kubernetes Secret named `keystone-db` by one static `ExternalSecret` (`deploy/eso/externalsecrets/keystone-db.yaml`, namespace `openstack`). Both the MariaDB `User` CR (`buildUser`, `operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_database.go`) and the derived connection string (`reconcileDBConnectionSecret`, `operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_dbconnection_secret.go`) read that Secret through `keystone.Spec.Database.SecretRef`. In a multi-tenant deployment — one operator fleet managing many ControlPlanes — every tenant's Keystone resolves to the *same* source secret, so rotating or compromising it hits every Keystone at once. This breaks the per-CR isolation the rest of the secret layout already enforces, and it is exactly the `Kubernetes Secrets Management` / `Secure by Design and Default` failure mode: a shared-blast-radius credential where a per-tenant one is cheap.

<commit-best-practices>
<subject-line>
  <rule name="format">"plan(CC-0116): <short description>"</rule>
  <rule name="types">feat | fix | test | refactor | docs | style | chore</rule>
  <rule name="length">Max 50 chars recommended, 72 chars absolute maximum</rule>
  <rule name="style">Imperative mood ("add" not "added", "fix" not "fixed")</rule>
  <rule name="punctuation">No period at end, capitalize after colon</rule>
</subject-line>

<body optional="true">
  <rule>Blank line required between subject and body</rule>
  <rule>Wrap lines at 72 characters maximum</rule>
  <rule>Explain WHAT changed and WHY (not HOW)</rule>
</body>

<avoid>
  <rule>Include "WIP", "temp", "test", or placeholder text</rule>
  <rule>Commit unrelated changes in the same commit</rule>
  <rule>Use past tense ("added", "fixed", "changed")</rule>
  <rule>Include issue numbers without context</rule>
</avoid>

<never-stage>
  NEVER stage or commit build/runtime artifacts. Before running `git add`,
  verify that NONE of these are included:
  - Python: __pycache__/, *.pyc, *.pyo, .venv/, venv/, .mypy_cache/,
    .ruff_cache/, .pytest_cache/, *.egg-info/, dist/, build/, .tox/, .nox/
  - Node.js: node_modules/, .next/, .turbo/, .parcel-cache/
  - Rust: target/, *.rlib
  - Go: *.test binary outputs
  - Compiled: *.exe, *.dll, *.so, *.dylib, *.o, *.obj, *.a, *.wasm
  - JVM: *.class, *.jar, *.war, *.ear
  - .NET: bin/, obj/, *.nupkg
  - Terraform: .terraform/, *.tfstate
  - OS: .DS_Store, Thumbs.db
  Use `git add <specific-files>` instead of `git add .` or `git add -A`.
  If in doubt, run `git status` first and only stage source files.
</never-stage>
</commit-best-practices>

<git-identity>
  <rule name="author">ALWAYS use --author flag: git commit --author "Christian Berendt <berendt@23technologies.cloud>" -m "..."</rule>
  <rule name="co-authored-by">Do NOT add any Co-Authored-By trailer. Never add "Co-Authored-By: Claude" or similar.</rule>
  <rule name="trailers">Append these trailers at the end of the commit message body, separated by a blank line:
    AI-assisted: Claude Code
    On-behalf-of: @SAP christian.berendt@sap.com
    Signed-off-by: Christian Berendt <berendt@23technologies.cloud>
  </rule>
</git-identity>


<output-format>
OUTPUT ONLY THE COMMIT MESSAGE, nothing else. No markdown formatting.

</output-format>
